project.title: WAAWer Coaster
project.description: WAAWer Coaster is a cozy toon roller coaster builder that runs in the browser. You lay track piece by piece across a living cartoon valley, close the circuit, send the train, and listen to the riders shout. Every model, sound and song is made in code. No downloads, no asset files.

project.title: Zemi
project.summary: Zemi is our website for seminar
project.description: Zemi is a weekly seminar run by MGM Laboratory. Every Friday from 13:15 to 15:15 WIB, Master’s and PhD students share research in progress, undergrads see what research looks like from the inside, and everyone gets better at asking questions. It happens in a classroom or a theater on campus and on the livestream at the same time. It is free, it is friendly, and nobody is grading you.

project.description: NeuroClash GG is a web-based edutainment platform that transforms conventional learning into a competitive auto-battler experience for students. The platform features an AI-powered question generator using the Gemini API to process PDFs into structured quizzes with answer keys and difficulty levels. It includes real-time 1v1 multiplayer battles with HP systems, damage calculation, and a StarBox comeback mechanic that gives losing players a chance to recover. Solo mode with an adaptive bot opponent and customizable.

project.title: Swara Ibu
project.summary: SwaraIbu is an AI-powered postpartum support mobile app that analyzes mothers’ voice and emotions to track mood, detect stress or crisis conditions, and provide personalized support with emergency alerts when needed.
project.description: Swara Ibu is a mobile application that supports mothers experiencing postpartum depression through voice-based emotional analysis and AI-powered crisis detection. Users express their feelings via voice input, which is processed using OpenAI Whisper for speech-to-text and Librosa for audio feature extraction to detect emotional distress. The app features mood tracking, companion access mode for family members, and Gemini AI-generated personalized support suggestions. Built during a 5-day hackathon using Kotlin and J

project.title: Numeracy Education Game
project.summary: Who says learning numbers has to be boring? 🎮 This paper explores how a fun educational game can help kindergarteners understand numbers while making learning feel like playtime!
project.coverAlt: Source visual from Perancangan Gim Edukasi Anak Usia Dini untuk Meningkatkan Pemahaman Pengenalan Angka
project.description: Learning numbers can be as fun as playing a game! 🎲 This paper introduces an educational game designed to help kindergarteners discover and understand numbers through interactive play. Using the MDA Framework, the researchers created a game that balances learning and fun. The results? Students' average test scores jumped from 41.67% to 75%, while the game received a fun rating of 4.48 out of 5. A playful approach to making early math learning more enjoyable and effective!

content.text: AnonChat is a self-hosted, anonymous, end-to-end encrypted messaging inbox. Anyone can create an anonymous identity — no email, phone number, or account required — and get a private, persistent conversation with the site owner.

Message content, attachments, and reactions are end-to-end encrypted: the server only ever stores and relays ciphertext. The owner gets a Discord/WhatsApp-style admin dashboard with every conversation, real-time replies over WebSocket, and moderation tools.
Stack

A pnpm monorepo split into crypto, shared, server, and web packages: a React front end talking to a Fastify + Prisma/PostgreSQL backend over WebSocket, with Argon2 password hashing, TOTP two-factor auth for the owner's dashboard, and S3-backed attachment storage.

content.text: A centralized, internal digital asset library for the MGM research lab and its partners — teams share Unity packages, Unreal projects, 2D/3D models, VFX, audio, animations, tools, and scripts through a web catalog, with companion Unity and Unreal editor plugins talking to the same API.
What it does

Full asset lifecycle management (drafts, presigned multipart S3 uploads, publish, archive, restore, ownership transfer), a BullMQ-driven file-analysis pipeline that extracts metadata from engine and 3D formats, Blender-to-glTF conversion with auto-generated thumbnails, ClamAV malware scanning with quarantine flows, and Meilisearch-backed catalog search.
A full admin panel handles moderation, featured slots, categories/tags/licenses, audit logging, and storage rollups, backed by typed real-time notifications over WebSocket and email.

project.title: Kit-Build Concept
project.summary: What if online learning felt more like solving a puzzle together? 🧩 This paper explores how collaborative concept mapping can make English reading comprehension more interactive, meaningful, and effective!
project.description: Learning English online doesn’t have to feel like a solo activity! 📚 This paper introduces a real-time collaborative learning approach using Kit-Build concept maps, where students work together to organize ideas, discuss concepts, and improve their English reading comprehension. By comparing it with traditional concept mapping, the researchers found that Kit-Build encouraged more meaningful discussions and better learning outcomes. A promising way to make online learning more collaborative, engaging, and effective

content.text: Atlas is a self-hostable organization workspace — one platform that replaces the usual stack of project-management and communication tools. Browse projects with tags, phases, and recruiting status through media-rich project pages, then coordinate the work in the same place.
What's inside

Slack-style project and global channels with threads, reactions, pins, and full-text search; a ClickUp-style PMO with lists, kanban, Gantt, collaborative notes and whiteboards (via Yjs), files, and dependencies; and Discord-style voice and video rooms with screen share, powered by LiveKit.
Twenty-four themes with light and dark palettes, a full RBAC permission system, and a "Godmode" control plane for self-hosted onboarding and instance configuration.

content.text: A smartphone-based, in-situ authoring tool for placing and storing outdoor location-based augmented-reality content with VSLAM and Google Street View reference data. This evidence-led showcase is built from the linked publication records; it distinguishes documented implementation details from claims the papers do not establish.
What the published work documents
The tool lets an author work at a point of interest on a smartphone, capture movement and surroundings, and place a virtual object without a desktop-first authoring workflow.
The published approach combines visual-inertial sensing, VSLAM, and Google Street View imagery to improve outdoor localization and AR-anchor alignment.
In the reported 15-participant authoring study, all participants completed the task; the paper reports a mean of 16.76 seconds to create one AR object in a 50 m radius area.

Batch 4: pedestrian location AR information support

This 2019 paper evaluates a location-based Android AR navigation prototype for bus-stop information in Zhongli District, Taiwan. It is related to the broader outdoor-LAR project family through its user-centred AR presentation work, but it is a distinct research prototype—not evidence of a current bus-navigation service, a live timetable, or a public authoring release.

The prototype uses a three-tier arrangement: the client requests data through a web service, application-server logic is separated from the database, and the client combines returned POI records with phone location, orientation, and movement sensors. A selected route supplies the scoped bus-stop objects. Haversine calculation provides distance; virtual markers are superimposed over corresponding physical locations.

props.caption: Step-by-step AR guidance with turn direction, destination side, and remaining distance. Source: Brata, Liang, and Dey (2019), Fig. 5a.

content.text: Rather than show all available POIs at once, the design shows the next waypoint and final target, includes direction arrows and distance, hides farther markers that compete in the same direction, and changes the target icon within 20 m. These mechanisms respond to the study’s finding that dense, simultaneous AR labels are difficult to interpret.

props.caption: AR bus-stop marker with distance and refresh control. Source: Brata, Liang, and Dey (2019), Fig. 5b.

content.text: Ten Android-experienced participants aged 20–28 completed blind and directed search tasks with standard location AR and the proposed system. Both conditions had 100% success in the reported table. Mean blind-search time was 5.40 minutes with the proposed presentation versus 14.9 standard; directed-search time was 5.12 versus 7.86 minutes. Questionnaire means also favoured the prototype, including 94 versus 73.6 for finding a location faster and 95 versus 79.3 for overall satisfaction.

This was a small field prototype in one Taiwanese transport context. Participants still reported AR drift and imperfect object alignment, even where the on-screen guidance helped them infer the right place. The paper does not establish city-wide accuracy, real-time transport information, current availability, or a maintained download/API. Its reported improvements are for the stated task comparison, not a general AR-navigation guarantee.
Batch 4 source scope
An Effective Approach to Develop Location-Based Augmented Reality Information Support (International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering, 2019), DOI: 10.11591/ijece.v9i4.pp3060-3068.
Batch 5: maps and AR as complementary pedestrian interfaces

This 2020 field study compares a 2D digital map interface with location-based AR for pedestrian navigation in Zhongli District, Taiwan. Ten Android-experienced students aged 20–28 completed blind and directed searches with both interfaces, using different but equally distant POIs to reduce route-learning effects. This is a small comparative prototype study, not evidence that either interface is a current navigation product.

Both interfaces achieved 100% task success. The digital map was modestly faster: blind search averaged 4.99 minutes versus 5.45 for AR; directed search 4.91 versus 5.20. UEQ-S pragmatic quality also favoured the map (1.90 versus 1.53), while AR was higher on hedonic quality (1.48 versus .53) and slightly higher overall (1.50 versus 1.21). The authors’ conclusion is nuanced: maps remain more familiar and practically efficient, whereas AR’s real-world overlay is more novel and engaging.

The authors caution that AR still needs usability improvements before it can be considered a substitute for traditional maps, and call for more respondents. This page therefore presents AR as a complementary presentation approach, without inventing a download, live transport feed, or operational pedestrian-navigation service.
Batch 5: BusAR route-information prototype

The earlier 2017 BusAR paper describes a three-tier Android prototype that overlays selected-route bus-stop POIs on the phone camera view. The client requests JSON through a RESTful web service, combines returned data with GPS, orientation, accelerometer, and gyroscope input, then places markers by direction and great-circle distance. Selecting a marker was designed to expose route information such as arrival time and fare.

Its evaluation and comparisons are specific to the study’s selected route and earlier systems. The paper does not establish present-day timetable accuracy, a current app, persistent backend, city-wide coverage, or public download. The project retains it as foundational AR information-support research.

project.summary: Ever seen AR content floating in the wrong place? 📍 This paper explores how Google Street View and visual tracking can make outdoor augmented reality more accurate, immersive, and reliable.
project.coverAlt: Source visual from A Proposal of In Situ Authoring Tool with Visual-Inertial Sensor Fusion for Outdoor Location-Based Augmented Reality
project.description:
Augmented reality is amazing, but what happens when virtual objects don’t line up with the real world? This paper introduces a smarter way to improve outdoor AR positioning using Visual SLAM and Google Street View instead of relying solely on GPS and compass sensors.

By testing different real-world locations, the researchers found significant improvements in positioning accuracy, helping virtual content appear exactly where it should. A promising step toward smoother, more immersive outdoor AR experiences!
